Simulate natural convection in a 2D square cavity using the de Vahl Davis benchmark configuration.
The cavity is filled with air.
The cavity is a square with side length L = 1 m.
Use the solver buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam.
Apply the Boussinesq approximation for buoyancy.
Gravity acts in the -y direction with g = (0 -9.81 0).
The left wall is hot with a fixedValue temperature boundary condition of T = 300 K.
The right wall is cold with a fixedValue temperature boundary condition of T = 290 K.
The top and bottom walls are adiabatic and use the zeroGradient temperature boundary condition.
All walls use the noSlip velocity boundary condition.
Use air properties with Prandtl number Pr = 0.71.
Set the temperature difference to ΔT = 10 K.
Tune the kinematic viscosity ν and thermal expansion coefficient β so that the Rayleigh number Ra = gβΔTL³/(να) = 10⁶ is achieved.
Target the de Vahl Davis (1983) benchmark results for Ra = 10⁶, including the average Nusselt number Nu_avg ≈ 1.725, for validation.
